1.explanation: The key bug element is the WebGLTileLayer class in src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js. This class is responsible for managing the WebGLTile layer and currently lacks a setStyle method or equivalent functionality to update the style after creation. The parseStyle function is also relevant because it constructs the shaders and uniforms from the style object; any dynamic style updating would need to use or re-invoke this logic. Adding a setStyle method to WebGLTileLayer (which would update this.style_, rebuild the renderer, and trigger a re-render) would address the bug. The renderer and style files do not expose setStyle-like APIs for WebGLTileLayer, so changes are needed in this class and possibly related utility functions like parseStyle.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario is that the WebGLTile layer in the OpenLayers library does not have a setStyle method. This means developers cannot dynamically change the visualization (such as shaders or style expressions) of a WebGLTile layer without removing and recreating the entire layer. This is problematic for use cases like dynamically updating the visualization of already loaded raster data (e.g., GeoTIFFs), where removing and re-adding the layer would unnecessarily reload data.

2.explanation: The core of the bug is the missing ability to set or update the style of a WebGLTileLayer after its initialization. The WebGLTileLayer class in src/ol/layer/WebGLTile.js is the main class for WebGL tile layers and manages the style through its style_ property but lacks a setStyle method. The parseStyle function is responsible for converting a style object into shader programs and uniforms, so any dynamic style application would need to interact with or re-run this logic. The createRenderer method is where the renderer is (re-)created based on the current style, so it must be called (or its logic used) when the style is changed. The existing updateStyleVariables method allows updating variables in the style but does not allow replacing the entire style logic. Therefore, to support setStyle, changes would likely be needed in WebGLTileLayer to add a setStyle method, which would update style_, possibly re-run parseStyle, and trigger renderer recreation or update. Other files and classes (such as Style in src/ol/style/Style.js) are not directly related since the WebGLTileLayer uses its own style object, not ol/style/Style instances.
2.bug_scenario: The bug scenario is that the WebGLTile layer in the application does not currently provide a method to dynamically change the style of the layer (such as updating the rendered appearance via a setStyle method), unlike other visualization properties or other layer types. This means users cannot update the visual styling of a WebGLTile layer without removing and re-adding the layer, which is inefficient and results in losing any already loaded raster data. This is particularly problematic for use-cases where users want to experiment with or update the visual representation of raster data (e.g., GeoTIFFs) on the fly.
